executiveSummary: GM1884 is identity-correct, deterministic and numerically complete across ten presets, six checkpoints and eight services, but is not a calibrated Kaag en Braassem first-72-hour forecast. The municipality is a low, pump-dependent mosaic of polders, boezem water, lakes, regional defences, bridges and ferries. Veiligheidsregio Hollands Midden explicitly distinguishes catastrophic primary-defence failure from more probable regional-defence failure caused by high boezem level or instability. The canonical coastal preset instead applies a broad 1.606538 legacy flood amplitude and 14,946 affected people-equivalent at T+24 without selecting a North Sea boundary, primary defence failure, connected footprint or recession; the major-river preset separately applies a persistent 0.553511 amplitude through T+72 without a named Rhine/Meuse/IJssel reach. Eight unrelated presets reuse the same top-five neighbourhood order. Public data identify 95 water-control points, a single sampled Liander planning area, 59 antenna sites, 13 education records, no local acute-care facility, and important A4/N207/bridge/ferry dependencies, but do not provide live operation or restoration. Unsupported direct flood precision must be suppressed or replaced by a named LIWO/Rijnland scenario. Missing water, road, utility, care and action state remains Unknown or NoData, never zero, safe, open or available.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: GM1884 official 2025 statistics, generalized geography, BAG places and neighbourhoods
evidenceSources.edition: CBS 2025; BAG/PDOK and BRT snapshots retrieved 31 August 2026
supports: Annual CC BY 4.0 CBS data identify GM1884 as Kaag en Braassem and report 29,316 residents, density 464 per square kilometre, 22.3% aged 65 or older and 4,060 one-person households. Rounded, suppressed, unavailable and not-applicable fields retain distinct null/zero semantics.

The municipal reference point [4.63199575226029, 52.188313249756966] lies inside the 2025 generalized multipolygon. Ten active BAG woonplaatsen—Hoogmade, Kaag, Leimuiden, Nieuwe Wetering, Oud Ade, Oude Wetering, Rijnsaterwoude, Rijpwetering, Roelofarendsveen and Woubrugge—are contained; BRT additionally labels three small settlements, including Bilderdam, Ofwegen and Vriezekoop under its own classification.

The 27 neighbourhood populations sum to 29,305, 11 below the municipal total (-0.038%); generated allocation reconciles exactly to 29,316. Registers omit event-time tourists, water recreation, greenhouse workers, ferry users, commuters, hospital patients, home-care dependency and household stocks.

evidenceSources.title: NWB, rail and scheduled public-transport inputs for Kaag en Braassem
evidenceSources.edition: NWB 1 August 2026; ProRail/OVapi snapshots retrieved 31 August–3 September 2026
supports: Monthly CC0 NWB geometry generates seven logical links: A4 north to Haarlemmermeer and south to Leiderdorp, N207 to Haarlemmermeer and Alphen aan den Rijn, N446 to Nieuwkoop and Leiderdorp, and N445 to Leiderdorp. Each paired road shares one physical corridor; generalized 260/150 capacities and series edges are non-additive scenario ceilings, not measured traffic or emergency throughput.

No ProRail station is inside GM1884. GTFS preprocessing finds 67 stop areas in a dispersed ten-village municipality. Geometry and schedules do not establish event-time bus/ferry operation, bridge state, evacuation throughput, fuel, staffing, hospital access or restoration.

No current NDW situation in the deployment's 2 September 2026 bounded snapshot is assigned to GM1884. That time/coverage output cannot be interpreted as every A4/N-road, local bridge or ferry approach being open.

evidenceSources.title: Regionaal Risicoprofiel Hollands Midden
evidenceSources.edition: Current fourth regional risk profile; 2027–2030 revision in preparation during 2026
supports: The profile distinguishes primary-defence breach from regional-defence breach. It describes primary failure as extremely unlikely and dependent on a very severe northwesterly storm plus extreme sea level, while regional failure can result from high boezem levels or dike instability and has a smaller but potentially serious footprint.

It identifies extreme cold/snow/ice, heat/smog, drought, storm/wind and extreme precipitation, and notes that low terrain, densification and subsidence can amplify effects. Its water-incident page explicitly includes Kaag en Braassem and notes that water incidents can require boats and cross-regional response.

This is regional planning/governance evidence, not a GM1884 event footprint, current warning, intervention state, numeric impact curve or restoration commitment. No blanket machine reuse licence was stated.

evidenceSources.title: Omgevingsvisie, Braassemerland water structure, bridges/ferries and current Leimuiderbrug dependency
evidenceSources.edition: Current official pages and adopted planning documents inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The municipality lists a 24-hour vehicle ferry between Kaag and Buitenkaag, seasonal/limited Oude Wetering and Paddegat services, and multiple operated or self-operated bridges. Kaag has no bridge or ring road; its ferry and narrow Julianalaan form the island's road access. Published schedules and normal-day planning capacity do not guarantee emergency operation.

On 12 August 2026 the municipality reported four Leimuiderbrug N207 outages in twelve days, each making this important Ringvaart connection unavailable for extended periods and disrupting residents, business, public transport and through traffic. This is a dated observed dependency, not a future closure forecast.

The 2016 Braassemerland water plan says the Braassemermeer boezem level is about 0.9 m above polder level and identifies the Galgekade/Noordkade regional defence, mixed and pressure sewers, broad waterways and bridges. Its historic project calculation and protection statement cannot establish current condition or municipality-wide impact.

The adopted 2024 environment vision includes design requirements for water nuisance, heat stress, subsidence and drought. Planning policy does not provide event-time exposure, action, resources or a blanket reuse licence.

evidenceSources.publisher: Hoogheemraadschap van Rijnland / Het Waterschapshuis / Rijkswaterstaat / WMCN
evidenceSources.title: Rijnland polder, boezem, defence and pump context plus public water-data routes
evidenceSources.edition: Current project pages; HWH/Waterinfo snapshots 2–3 September 2026; LIWO release 2025.1.6
supports: Rijnland describes the 359-hectare Veender- and Lijkerpolder outside the embankment, containing a large part of built Roelofarendsveen, as bounded by Braassemermeer and neighbouring polders and requiring measures for heavier short rain and longer drought. A separate Witte Singel section along the lake requires strengthening; the completed DAHB work and current Gogerpolder/Doespolder pump replacements show changing assets, not failure or guaranteed protection.

The deployed CC BY-SA 4.0 HWH collections contain 95 GM1884 points: 81 surface-water pumps, ten sewer pumps, two sluices and two wastewater plants. Fifty-two have non-null capacity and 43 are null; 83 name Rijnland and twelve use generic manager 'Waterschap'. Units/topology, operation, backup, current status and comparable spare capacity are not established.

No Waterinfo observation or forecast point is assigned within GM1884 in the bounded snapshots. Public Waterinfo observation/forecast coverage is point-based and declines by horizon; an empty local or T+72 result is NoData, not zero water, normality or an all-clear.

LIWO release 2025.1.6 at https://basisinformatie-overstromingen.nl/geoserver/ows is an irregular expert scenario library. A governed run must retain selected release/scenario, source water and boundary hydrograph/level/datum, primary or regional defence section/state, breach/overtopping, connected footprint, depth/velocity/arrival/recession, probability, resolution, per-layer licence, coverage and NoData; it is not a live observation.

evidenceSources.publisher: Stichting Mijn Aansluiting / Netbeheer Nederland / RDI / DUO / RIVM
evidenceSources.title: Public provider territories, grid planning, communications, education and acute-care context
evidenceSources.edition: Provider/register/planning snapshots retrieved in 2026; RIVM acute-care v1.1
supports: The Public Domain Mijn Aansluiting WMS identifies Liander electricity/gas, Oasen drinking water and Ziggo media at the municipal reference point; provider dates range from September 2025 to March 2026 and drainage returns empty. A point territory lookup is not municipality-wide completeness, topology, outage, quality, capacity or restoration.

The single sampled Liander area OS LEIMUIDEN 10-2i reports 35 MW existing/26 MW required withdrawal plus 3.2 MW and 12 queued requests, 57 MW existing/32 MW required injection plus 12 MW and five queued requests, and eleven projects earliest 2026. NBNL planning is at least quarterly and queues monthly; its exact dataset licence was not found. It is not current load, household availability, reserve or T+72 state.

RDI WFS returns 59 antenna sites, including 26 mobile and 16 fixed-link sites; no fixed refresh or reuse licence was stated. Daily DUO RIO under CC BY (version unspecified) returns 13 education records. These do not prove radio coverage/backhaul/power, shelter role, occupancy, staff, supplies or live status.

RIVM acute-care questionnaire v1.1, published 3 July 2026 under CC0, assigns no acute-care point to GM1884. Empty local count is not no acute-care need and does not establish which facility accepts a patient during an event.

evidenceSources.publisher: Alrijne Ziekenhuis / RIVM / Nationaal Coördinator Terrorismebestrijding en Veiligheid
evidenceSources.title: Cross-boundary acute care and national first-72-hour preparedness guidance
evidenceSources.edition: Current hospital page; RIVM questionnaire v1.1; NCTV information booklet published 4 March 2026
supports: Alrijne says its Leiderdorp emergency department is open 24 hours a day, seven days a week. RIVM identifies it as 24/7 SEH plus acute obstetrics with 20 reported treatment rooms and 33,265 visits in 2025. This establishes a plausible cross-boundary dependency over the A4/N446 network, not event-time acceptance, beds, staffing, backup duration, oxygen, medicines or route availability.

NCTV's Denk vooruit guidance at https://www.denkvooruit.nl/informatieboekje advises households to manage 72 hours with a kit, plan and mutual help, including three litres of water per person per day. It also says incidents can last longer and responders cannot be everywhere at once.

Annual registration and preparedness advice are not causal restoration inputs, a measurement of household stocks, or a promise that care, roads, ferries, utilities or supplies recover by T+72. No blanket reuse licence was identified on the hospital/guidance pages.

identity.summary: Official code, name, province, safety region, centre and headline demography agree.
notes: GM1884 is uniquely Kaag en Braassem in Zuid-Holland and Veiligheidsregio Hollands-Midden.
Boundary/statistics editions are 2025; project status, August 2026 bridge incidents, current registers and the synthetic clock remain separate.
The reference point is contained and no headline mismatch was found.

geography.summary: Municipal geometry is coherent, but polder, boezem, lake, defence and island access mechanisms require full-resolution source geometry.
notes: Official evidence distinguishes primary-defence failure from regional boezem-defence failure and identifies multiple polder/lake/pump pathways.
A municipal centroid, coast/river-distance screen or shared neighbourhood seed cannot replace defence sections, hydraulic connectivity, AHN terrain, pumps, bridges and ferry geometry.
Every LIWO/Rijnland/HWH/planning layer needs its own edition, valid time, resolution, licence, coverage and NoData mask.

demography.summary: Official 2025 totals agree and neighbourhood rounding is explicitly reconciled.
notes: Population 29,316, density 464, age65Pct 22.3 and one-person households 4,060 agree.
Neighbourhood population sums to 29,305 (-11); generated allocation reconciles to 29,316. Published households total 12,860 and age65+ rows total 6,540.
Dispersed-village and older-resident context does not measure who needs evacuation, transport, medicines, cooling or care.

regionalDetail.summary: All 27 neighbourhoods load, but statistics, water-system coverage and operational state are incomplete.
notes: District heat and charging are missing for 27/27; home value and housing/tenure for two; cars per household for seven; benefit fields for three. Null is not zero.
HWH supplies 95 water points, but 43 capacities are null and non-null values cannot be summed without units, topology and current state.
Provider, planning, antenna, education and acute-care records do not establish event-time availability.

settlements.summary: Ten BAG woonplaatsen and thirteen BRT settlement labels form a coherent dispersed settlement context.
notes: All ten BAG centres are contained; BRT adds two buurtschappen and recognizes eleven woonkernen under distinct source semantics.
Settlement labels are not independent population counts and must not duplicate neighbourhood allocation.
Kaag island, harbour/lake recreation and seasonal visitors require separate event-time occupancy and access state.

transport.summary: National roads are reproducible, but critical bridge, ferry, island and hospital access are absent from the causal network.
notes: Seven boundary edges represent four paired physical A4/N-road corridors and are non-additive; internal bridges, ferries and local approaches are absent.
The 24-hour Kaag ferry is its vehicle access but a schedule is not emergency availability; other ferries are seasonal or limited.
Recent repeated Leimuiderbrug N207 outages demonstrate a material crossing dependency that the empty NDW snapshot and generic route ceiling do not represent.
No station is inside the municipality; Alrijne Leiderdorp access and destination acceptance are Unknown.

emergencyContext.summary: Authorities, flood mechanisms, mobility dependencies, cross-boundary care and 72-hour guidance are identified, but no auditable action/resource state exists.
notes: The model lacks selected primary/regional defence, boezem level, pump/sluice/bridge/ferry state, warning trigger, authority, resource and completion.
Alrijne is a plausible regional SEH dependency, not guaranteed capacity; access, power, water, telecom, staffing, oxygen, medicines and acceptance remain Unknown.

Required actions include warning, defence/boezem/pump decisions, evacuation/reception, bridge/ferry/road control, care continuity, temporary water/sanitation, greenhouse/livestock and household supply, utility repair and mutual aid.
National 72-hour advice is not measured local preparedness or a recovery deadline.

scenarioMatrix.summary: All ten presets return complete finite deterministic results at all six checkpoints and eight services; realism failures are separate.
notes: Mandatory and focused gates covered ten presets at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 for power, water, drainage, gas, telecom, mobility, facilities and supply.

Outputs are synthetic exercise indices; affected people-equivalent is not observed people/casualties and person-hours is cumulative weighted local pre-network service shortfall versus a matched baseline.

numericalInvariants.summary: Determinism, bounds, zero-event baseline, reconciliation and monotonic burden contracts pass.
notes: Initial MUNICIPALITY_AUDIT_CODE=GM1884 pnpm audit:model passed both tests across the complete matrix.
Intensity-zero event effects are zero, repeat runs and UI/core presets agree, and local allocation reconciles exactly.
Service-layer selection preserves physical hazard, route ceilings hold and event-attributable person-hours is monotonic.
Arithmetic correctness does not establish local calibration.

spatialPlausibility.summary: Broad unselected flood mechanisms and repeated neighbourhood order contradict source-specific primary, boezem, polder and mobility pathways.
notes: Coastal T+24 applies legacy flood amplitude 1.606538 and 14,946 affected people-equivalent without sea level/storm, primary defence failure, breach, connected footprint, arrival or recession.

River T+24 and T+72 retain amplitude 0.553511 and severity 0.174877 without a named Rhine/Meuse/IJssel reach; actual Oude Rijn/boezem and regional-defence mechanisms are separately typed and unresolved.

Storm, pluvial, river, coastal, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire share Oude Wetering, Rijnsaterwoude, Nieuwe Wetering, Woubrugge and Roelofarendsveen-Noord as the T+24 top five. Their order is therefore not evidence of water, heat, wind, cyber or fire exposure.
Canonical wildfire has zero direct fire, 0.326144 smoke and 0.677683 drought, affecting 29 people-equivalent without ignition, fuel, plume or time-valid fire-risk input.

serviceDependencies.summary: Exact service percentages are inspectable but not calibrated to Rijnland pumps, utilities, crossings, villages or Alrijne.
notes: Coastal T+24 availability is power 41.76%, water 42.26%, drainage 21.78%, gas 67.96%, telecom 36.29%, mobility 76.29%, facilities 50.91% and supply 62.19%; no authority/operator validates these values.
Liander/Oasen/Ziggo territory, one NBNL sample, HWH assets and RDI sites remain non-causal context.
NWB omits pump/utility topology and internal bridge/ferry dependencies; Alrijne registration does not establish access, backup or incident capacity.
Sensitive or unavailable topology must use explicit aggregate synthetic fallback, never invented public precision.

causalTrace.summary: Evidence classes are present but unresolved water, defence, crossing, target and operational dimensions are not declared.
notes: Coastal and river report derived-screening, while compound reports synthetic with unsupportedDimensions=[], despite no selected boundary level, defence, breach, footprint, pumps, crossings or recession.
The legacy floodDepthM values must not be presented as surveyed metres.
Cyber lacks a target; wildfire lacks ignition/fuel/plume. Current, incident, annual planning/register and synthetic T+72 times cannot be fused.
Empty Waterinfo, NDW, drainage-provider and local acute-care output must become explicit NoData/Unknown, not normal, open, safe or available.

recovery72h.summary: Coastal, river and compound residual impacts lack hydraulic, operator, crossing, hospital or action evidence.
notes: Coastal direct severity returns to zero by T+72, yet pressure is 0.214570, affected people-equivalent 3,080 and person-hours 1,037,916.38; drainage remains 0.606546 and facilities 0.682314 without recession/dewatering or restoration evidence.
River T+72 retains severity 0.174877 and amplitude 0.553511; affected rises from 3,563 to 4,117 while facilities fall from 0.788089 to 0.692146, without a selected event or action.
Compound affected rises from 13,228 at T+24 to 14,357 at T+72 and facilities falls from 0.624907 to 0.429567 while the other seven service values plateau exactly.

No defence/pump decision, road/bridge/ferry reopening, utility crew, Alrijne acceptance, household stock or confirmed intervention supports those curves; 72 hours is a preparedness horizon, not an all-recovered promise.

findings.summary: The coastal preset presents an unselected primary-defence failure as precise municipality-wide flooding.
findings.evidence: Coastal T+24 reports legacy flood amplitude 1.606538 and 14,946 affected people-equivalent. VRHM says primary failure requires very specific extreme sea/storm conditions, but the run names no boundary, defence, breach, footprint, probability, timing or recession.
findings.action: Suppress direct coastal impact and precise affected/service attribution unless an expert-selected versioned LIWO primary-defence scenario intersects GM1884. Preserve sea level/hydrograph/datum, storm, defence/breach state, connected footprint, depth/velocity/arrival/recession, probability, licence, coverage and NoData.

findings.summary: The major-river preset conflates Rhine/Meuse/IJssel forcing with Oude Rijn/boezem and regional-defence risk.
findings.evidence: River T+24/T+72 reports persistent 0.553511 legacy flood amplitude without a named major-river reach. Local source evidence instead describes boezem-fed lakes/waterways, pump-dependent polders and regional kering failure driven by high boezem or instability.
findings.action: Suppress direct GM1884 major-river impact in the generic Rhine/Meuse/IJssel preset. Add a separately typed Rijnland boezem/regional-defence event with selected level, defence section/state, connected footprint and timing; keep unresolved indirect effects and local water risk Unknown rather than safe.

findings.summary: One shared neighbourhood ranking substitutes for hazard-specific geometry.
findings.evidence: Eight unrelated presets reuse the same top-five order. Although the names include water-rich villages, identical heat, cyber, winter and wildfire ranking proves the order is not hydraulic validation and does not encode defences, polder elevation, pumps, heat, road access or ignition.
findings.action: Remove the common multiplier from physical hazard ranking. Show uniform unresolved municipal amplitude or Unknown until each hazard uses versioned geometry; test primary/regional flood, pluvial, heat and fire ranks independently.

findings.summary: Pluvial depth and impact precision lacks polder, greenhouse, sewer and pump calibration.
findings.evidence: Pluvial T+24 reports legacy amplitude 0.177990 and 1,045 affected people-equivalent. Official sources identify extreme-rain, subsidence, boezem, low-polder and pump dependencies, but no hyetograph, terrain, groundwater, drainage topology, operating pump state or connected footprint drives the result.
findings.action: Integrate Rijnland/municipal stress-test or 3Di output with rainfall hyetograph, AHN/BGT, polder/boezem boundaries, sewer-included flag, pump state, groundwater/saturation, resolution, edition/licence and NoData; otherwise label precise local depth/rank/affected unsupported.

findings.summary: Exact utility and recovery percentages have no operator evidence.
findings.evidence: Coastal and compound return eight exact availability curves. Liander/Oasen/Ziggo territory, one NBNL planning sample, HWH points and RDI registrations provide no live outage, topology, water quality, pump/control state, backup, switching, crew or repair evidence; drainage provider lookup is empty.
findings.action: Keep public layers affectsSimulation=false and label operational values aggregate synthetic/Unknown. Ingest only authorized time-scoped operator aggregates and preserve manual incident-override provenance; empty or null records never mean zero, safe or available.

findings.summary: Ninety-five water assets are high-value context but not an operational drainage model.
findings.evidence: HWH supplies 81 surface-water pumps, ten sewer pumps, two sluices and two wastewater plants; 43 capacities are null and non-null records lack comparable unit/topology/state semantics. Rijnland project pages show assets and defences changing over 2025–2027.
findings.action: Retain every point, manager, null, source collection, retrieval, licence and partial-coverage warning. Seek Rijnland-authorized catchment/control aggregates; never sum registered capacities or infer operating, backup or spare capacity.

findings.summary: Critical island, bridge and ferry dependencies are missing from first-72-hour mobility.
findings.evidence: Kaag depends on its vehicle ferry and narrow Julianalaan; several other ferries and movable bridges have limited schedules. Four Leimuiderbrug outages in twelve days in August 2026 show N207 crossing fragility, while NWB represents only boundary road corridors and the NDW snapshot is empty locally.
findings.action: Add critical crossing and approach identifiers with authority, event-valid open/restricted/closed/Unknown status, vehicle class, ferry hours/capacity and alternate route. Keep paired A4/N-road edges physically non-additive and route Alrijne access only over confirmed passable links.

findings.summary: Cross-boundary Alrijne acute-care access and acceptance are absent.
findings.evidence: No acute-care point lies in GM1884. RIVM and Alrijne establish a 24/7 SEH plus acute obstetrics at Leiderdorp, but not disaster-time acceptance, occupancy, staff, backup, oxygen, medicines or A4/N446/local crossing access.
findings.action: Add authorized aggregate facility role, live acceptance/diversion, access, backup/fuel, critical supply and transfer status with valid time. Empty local count remains cross-boundary dependency, not no demand; absent operational fields remain Unknown.

findings.summary: No auditable first-72-hour action/resource ledger represents water, transport, care and village dependencies.
findings.evidence: Public sources identify responsible authorities, flood mechanisms, many pumps/defences, crossings, a remote SEH and household guidance, but the simulator ingests no warning trigger, assignment, resources, state or completion.
findings.action: Add Unknown-first records for warning, defence/boezem/pump decisions, evacuation/reception, bridges/ferries/roads, hospital continuity/transfer, temporary water/sanitation, food/fuel/medicine, greenhouse/livestock needs, utility repair and mutual aid. Actions affect recovery only after confirmed status and provenance.

findings.summary: Non-flood hazard inclusion is bounded but not locally calibrated.
findings.evidence: Wildfire reports zero fire but synthetic smoke/drought; earthquake has zero direct ground motion but nonzero burden; storm, heat, winter and cyber use synthetic forcing and the common neighbourhood order. VRHM supports regional scenario inclusion, not these exact values or spatial patterns.
findings.action: Retain presets as clearly synthetic exercises with named target/ignition/valid-time weather where relevant. Do not describe zero direct earthquake/fire as an all-clear, or infer observed smoke, heat, ice, wind or cyber impact from bounded output.

corrections.summary: Suppress unsupported GM1884 major-river inundation and preserve Rijnland boezem/regional-water risk as separately Unknown.
corrections.validation: The generic Rhine/Meuse/IJssel preset produces zero GM1884 direct flood and direct affected population with an explicit unsupported-pathway note; separately typed Oude Rijn/boezem/regional-defence and indirect network risks remain Unknown rather than safe.

corrections.summary: Gate coastal inundation on a selected primary-defence event and add Rijnland regional-defence semantics.
corrections.validation: No precise coastal or regional-defence result appears without a named versioned scenario; supported fixtures retain water boundary/datum, storm, defence/breach/overtopping state, connected footprint, depth/velocity/arrival/recession, probability, licence, coverage and NoData.

corrections.summary: Replace common neighbourhood ranking with hazard-specific defence, polder, pluvial, heat and fire geometry.
corrections.validation: Unrelated presets no longer share one top-five order; flood fixtures follow selected connected defence scenarios, pluvial fixtures retain pump/sewer/groundwater semantics and unresolved hazards display Unknown rather than invented gradients.

corrections.summary: Keep water/provider/grid/antenna/education/acute-care records context-only with strict Unknown/NoData semantics.
corrections.validation: Cards/exports expose publisher, version, retrieval/valid time, licence, coverage and affectsSimulation=false; null capacities and empty Waterinfo, NDW, drainage-provider and local acute-care outputs never render as zero, normal, safe, open or available.

corrections.summary: Represent critical crossings, Alrijne and role-aware first-72-hour actions in an Unknown-first ledger.
corrections.validation: At every checkpoint defences/pumps, warning/evacuation, bridge/ferry/road access, hospital acceptance/transfer, reception/resupply and utility repair show authority, trigger, assignment, resource, state, source and valid time; only confirmed actions influence recovery.

residualLimitations: No reviewed public source provides complete safe-to-publish Liander/Oasen/gas/telecom/drainage topology, live control state, backup endurance, crews, inventories or restoration estimates.

Flood consequences depend on whether a primary or regional defence fails, the selected sea/boezem/lake level, breach location, polder connectivity, pumps, terrain and recession; project pages and generic screens are not event forecasts.
HWH asset completeness and capacity semantics vary; point geometry and registered values do not establish hydraulic topology, comparable throughput, operating state or spare capacity.
Bridge/ferry schedules and dated Leimuiderbrug outages do not establish future event-time access, vessel/bridge condition, emergency priority or alternate-route capacity.
CBS/BAG/BRT/DUO/RIVM records omit visitors, water recreation, greenhouse/livestock operations, commuters, home-care needs, live hospital load, shelters and household stocks.
Affected population is a people-equivalent scenario index and person-hours is weighted local service deprivation, not casualties, evacuations, patients or customer interruptions.
Current water, weather, road, warning and facility states may change after audit completion; stale or out-of-coverage inputs must degrade to Unknown.
provinceReviewFlags: Separate North Sea primary-defence, Rhine/Meuse/IJssel major-river and Rijnland boezem/regional-defence scenarios across Zuid-Holland; do not infer all three from centroid distance.

Reconcile Kaag en Braassem, Haarlemmermeer, Teylingen, Leiden/Leiderdorp, Nieuwkoop and Alphen water pathways using one versioned LIWO/Rijnland/RWS contract with explicit polder connectivity and NoData.
Suppress GM1884's generic major-river false positive and gate its broad coastal output on a selected primary-defence failure.
Test shared neighbourhood-ranking defects across lake/polder, greenhouse, urban, heat and rural contexts with hazard-specific surfaces.
Audit A4/N207/N445/N446, Leimuiderbrug, Kaag ferry and other bridge/ferry dependencies without double-counting paired road edges or converting schedules into guaranteed capacity.
Represent Alrijne Leiderdorp and other regional care destinations through event-valid access/acceptance, and require Unknown-first 72-hour water, evacuation, reception, resupply and repair actions.
